To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of the yeast copper chap-eron yCCS in combination with a Cu(2+)/Zn(2+) supplemented medium allows for the efficient overproduction of human CuZnS-OD and the CuZn-superoxyde dismutase variants D90A, F50E/GS1E, and G93A, all with full metal contents and with high specific activities.
the use of a copper chaperone in combination with Cu(2+)- and Zn(2+) -supplemented growth media allows the expression of CuZn-superoxyde dismutase variants with high metal contents in E. coli.

the use of the copper chaperone yeast Cu, Zn-SOD (yCCS), in conjunction with the copper chaperones human Cu,Zn-SOD (hCCS) and PseudoEC-Cu,Zn-SOD, is a simple and effective strategy to produce recombinant Cu,Zn-SODe with high copper contents in E. coli.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a system that can be used for the production of Cu- and Zn-superoxide dis-mutases with high Cu contents, which is essential for studies of the function of these proteins in normal and diseased cells.

the development of a system that allows overexpression of CuZn-SODs with high copper contents, which is important for the understanding of the function and role of these enzymes in normal and disorded cells.
a new approach to the expression, characterization, and purification of CuZn-superoxoide dismutases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SOD variants produced with this system are suitable for detailed studies of Cu- and Zn-binding properties and for the investigation of CuZnSODO2(+) interactions with other proteins.
this system provides an effective and simple method to produce SOD variants with high copper content and that the system can be used as a basis for the production of SOD variants with other metals.
the CuZn-supoxide dismutases were expressed in a functional state, with the Cu content being 1.0 +/- 0.2 atom per monomeric enzyme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CuZn-superoxide dismutases were overexpressed in the cytosolic space of E. coli with high copper contents, and that the recombinant enzymes were purified to high homogeneity.
this E. coli system is a powerful tool for the overproduction and purification of CuZnSod variants for structural and functional studies.
the E. coli-based coexpression system for the production of human CuZnSod with high Cu contents is highly efficient and can be recommended for the large-scale production of SOD enzymes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CuZn-SOD variants with full metal content were obtained in high yields and in good purity and can be used to study the role of CuZn-SO in oxidative stress, neurodegenerative diseases and cancer.
the E. coli system is suitable for the production of SOD variants with full metal content.

the E. coli system described herein can be applied to produce a variety of SOD enzymes, with high Cu contents, for structural, biochemical, and biophysical characterization, and for use in studies of protein-protein interactions and protein aggregation.
